title: Transcriber's Note Wording: Notes in a Separate Volume

illustrates.quote: An agency may request that notes be provided in a separate volume(s) when a book has text and notes on facing pages. In this situation, use combined page numbers in both volumes of text and notes. Indicate that the notes are in a separate volume on the Transcriber’s Notes page. Sample:

blocks.text: The text and the notes to the text are in separate volumes.
blocks.features: Set in italics, indented as a sample of suggested wording for the Transcriber's Notes page (not a worked print/braille pair with its own boxed illustration).

print.surroundingText: Follows rule 16.7.7a directly, illustrating rule 16.7.7 (Notes on Facing Pages) about text/notes split into separate volumes.
print.printFeatures: Plain indented italic sentence, no box, no accompanying braille rendering shown in the source.

braille.notes: No braille rendering of this sentence is given in the source -- it is offered only as suggested English wording for a Transcriber's Notes page entry, not as a worked print-to-braille example. None is guessed here.

uncertain: This item is a plain-text 'Sample:' of suggested wording (not a worked braille illustration); braille.lines is left empty rather than inferring a transcription.
resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.7.7.a per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: print-only per standards-map.md's own worked-examples table ("Has braille: No"); both runs agree. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
